name: SmartDocument
title: Smart Document
description: Produce a long-form deliverable — report, plan, spec, article, brief — that an agent writes and revises section by section instead of emitting one big blob. Section-addressed, hash-checked markdown edits (no drift, no full rewrites); live-renders on every edit.
whenToUse: Pick whenever an agent must author or revise a long document — report, plan, spec, article, brief. Writes and revises section by section and live-renders each edit; a one-shot generation can't be revised and blows the context window on every change. Attach via a service edge to an agent node, and route its markdown to a MarkdownRenderer to display.

package.name: smart-document
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# THE LAST HYBRID NODE, as a manifest. What actually needed code was the DOCUMENT ENGINE —
# sectionizing, hash-checked edits, WATCH/MULTI concurrency, the mutation-re-fires-renderer
# contract — and that is computation, which belongs to the executor (the awsSigV4 rule).
# It moved there whole (packages/base/src/manifests/runtime/docstore/, transcribed verbatim)
# and this package became a description: which tools exist, what they say to a model, and
# where the markdown lands. Design rationale: _legacy/nodes/smart-document/CLAUDE.md.
#
# NO allowedHosts, and that is not an omission: the node reaches no host at all. The
# document lives in the platform's own Redis, behind `docstore:` calls.

name: smart-document
displayName: Smart Document
description: A long markdown document an agent writes and revises section by section
version: 1.0.0
# `ai`, transcribed from the retired package.json — the PACKAGE vocabulary has no
# "documents"; that is the NODE vocabulary, where this node's category is Documents.
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Section-addressed, hash-checked markdown edits — no drift, no full rewrites
  - Live-renders on every edit through the hybrid re-fire
  - Survives across runs and chats, isolated per user, workflow and node instance

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.7.0"
  # The whole package. On an executor without the docstore every tool is missing at once,
  # and the failure would otherwise surface as a model politely reporting broken tools.
  docstore: true

files.api/events.yaml:
# The one connector: the whole document as markdown, exactly what the retired executor's
# executeNode emitted. A MarkdownRenderer downstream re-receives it on every mutation via
# the hybrid re-fire.

- emit: markdown
  value: "return response.markdown"
files.api/run.yaml:
# THE WORKFLOW HALF of the hybrid: when the graph runs this node — including the re-fire the
# executor performs after every mutating tool call — it renders the CURRENT document for a
# downstream renderer. `render` initialises from config when the doc is cold, so the very
# first run seeds initialMarkdown.
#
# The doc's KEY is derived by the executor from the run's own ids (user + workflow +
# conversation + node instance); this file could not name it if it tried.

- name: doc
  docstore: render
files.api/service.yaml:
# THE AGENT HALF of the hybrid: nine tools, each ONE docstore op. The op's arguments are the
# caller's params passed through untouched — validation, hash checks and error shaping live
# in the executor's docstore, so `returns` is simply the op's own result.
#
# A MUTATING op here re-fires the workflow channel after it returns (the executor detects
# the op in this very list), which is what keeps a downstream renderer showing the document
# the agent just edited. Read ops never re-fire — re-rendering on reads flooded the renderer
# once already.

getSchema:
  description: Tool discovery for the section-addressed markdown document
  calls: []
  returns: { $ref: schema#document }

outline:
  description: >-
    Return the list of sections with metadata. Call first in any session and whenever you
    suspect the document changed. Does not return full bodies.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: outline
  returns: "return calls.op"

readSection:
  description: >-
    Return the body of one section. Use the hash from outline() or a previous read as
    expectedHash in edits.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: readSection
  returns: "return calls.op"

updateSection:
  description: >-
    Replace heading and/or body of a section. For small edits on long sections, prefer
    replaceInSection. Body must not contain H1 or H2 headings.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: updateSection
  returns: "return calls.op"

appendToSection:
  description: Append text to the end of a section's body. Saves a read-modify-write.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: appendToSection
  returns: "return calls.op"

replaceInSection:
  description: >-
    Replace an exact substring inside one section's body. old_str must match exactly once.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: replaceInSection
  returns: "return calls.op"

insertSection:
  description: >-
    Create a new section, placed by exactly one of afterId, beforeId or parentId (omit all
    three to append at the end).
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: insertSection
  returns: "return calls.op"

deleteSection:
  description: Delete a section, cascading to descendants when asked.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: deleteSection
  returns: "return calls.op"

moveSection:
  description: Move a section to a new position without touching its content.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: moveSection
  returns: "return calls.op"

resetDoc:
  description: >-
    DESTRUCTIVE. Re-parse the config's initialMarkdown with fresh IDs, discarding all
    current content.
  calls:
    - name: op
      docstore: resetDoc
  returns: "return calls.op"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    initialMarkdown:
      type: string
      title: Initial content
      description: >-
        Seeded into Redis when the node first executes. Parsed into sections on init (H1/H2
        become sections; H3+ stays in bodies). Re-parsing a changed config does NOT reset an
        existing doc — the agent's resetDoc tool does, explicitly.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    sectionizeAt:
      type: number
      title: Sectionize at
      description: >-
        Which heading level starts a new section. 2 (default) = H1 and H2 are sections, H3+
        stays in bodies. 1 = only H1 is a section.
      default: 2
      enum: [1, 2]
      enumNames: ["H1 only", "H1 and H2"]

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    # Instance config, not the manifest's `auth`: the manifest is the node author's floor,
    # these are the builder's per box, and the executor takes the stricter of the two.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, initialMarkdown, sectionizeAt]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

# A HYBRID: the one output is the workflow half (the rendered markdown for a renderer), and
# the serviceConnector is the agent half (the editing tools). A MUTATING tool call re-fires
# the workflow channel, which is what keeps the two halves showing the same document.

inputs: []

outputs:
  - name: markdown
    type: string
    description: Current rendered markdown content

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    description: MCP tools for a single agent to read and edit this markdown document by section
    # `getSchema` is deliberately absent: it is tool DISCOVERY, a meta-method the harness
    # calls, not one of the tools on offer.
    methods:
      - outline
      - readSection
      - updateSection
      - appendToSection
      - replaceInSection
      - insertSection
      - deleteSection
      - moveSection
      - resetDoc
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: SmartDocument
kind: PromiseNode

name: Smart Document
category: Documents
color: "#10b981"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  Produce a long-form deliverable — report, plan, spec, article, brief — that an agent writes
  and revises section by section instead of emitting one big blob. Section-addressed,
  hash-checked markdown edits (no drift, no full rewrites); live-renders on every edit.

whenToUse: >-
  Pick whenever an agent must author or revise a long document — report, plan, spec, article,
  brief. Writes and revises section by section and live-renders each edit; a one-shot
  generation can't be revised and blows the context window on every change. Attach via a
  service edge to an agent node, and route its markdown to a MarkdownRenderer to display.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # The graph-triggered run renders CURRENT Redis state, which a service-channel mutation
  # changes between any two runs — a cached render is exactly the stale document the whole
  # hash discipline exists to prevent.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# The graph-triggered half: initialise from config, render the whole doc. The docstore
# normalizes blank-line spacing between sections (heading and body join with one blank
# line), so the assertion checks CONTENT presence rather than byte equality — byte-level
# round-trip was never the retired node's contract either.

testData:
  config:
    initialMarkdown: |
      # Plan

      The overview paragraph.

      ## First step

      Do the thing.
    sectionizeAt: 2
  inputs: {}
  expect:
    markdown: >-
      return output.markdown.includes('# Plan')
        && output.markdown.includes('## First step')
        && output.markdown.includes('Do the thing.')
